name: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for pancreatic mucinous cystadenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of mucin-producing epithelial malignant cells with stromal invasion
Radiologic evidence of cystic pancreatic mass with mural nodules or solid components on CT/MRI
Elevated serum CA 19-9 and/or CEA levels supportive of malignancy
Symptoms consistent with pancreatic malignancy such as abdominal pain or jaundice

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignancy plus radiologic evidence of cystic pancreatic mass with malignant features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological examination; imaging and tumor markers aid in clinical suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass in epigastric region
Mucinous cystic lesion with malignant features on imaging
searchTerms: cystic tumor with cancer signs on scan
jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile

occasional.symptomName: Back pain radiating to the spine
searchTerms: pain in back extending to spine
enlarged liver felt on exam due to spread
palpable liver enlargement from cancer spread

laboratory: Mild elevation of liver function tests in biliary obstruction
imaging: CT/MRI showing cystic pancreatic mass with mural nodules or solid enhancing components
Dilated pancreatic duct proximal to lesion
genetic: KRAS mutations frequently observed in tumor tissue
TP53 mutations associated with malignant transformation
other: Histopathology demonstrating mucin-producing malignant epithelial cells with stromal invasion
Presence of ovarian-type stroma in cyst wall (supportive of mucinous cystic neoplasm origin)

distinguishingFeatures: Serous cystadenocarcinoma typically presents with clear serous fluid rather than mucinous
Less common elevation of tumor markers CA 19-9 and CEA
Histology shows glycogen-rich cuboidal cells without mucin production
IPMN involves main pancreatic duct or branch ducts with papillary mucinous growth
Communication with pancreatic duct system seen on imaging
Different histological architecture with papillary projections

references: Adsay NV, et al. Mucinous cystic neoplasms of the pancreas: clinicopathologic features and prognosis. Am J Surg Pathol. 2004.
Tanaka M, et al. International consensus guidelines for management of IPMN and MCN of the pancreas. Pancreatology. 2012.
Kamisawa T, et al. Pancreatic cystic neoplasms: diagnosis and management. World J Gastroenterol. 2014.
